newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Tupolev 334 to start test flights in May.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Tupolev 334 to start test flights in May.

text.p: Russia's Aviatsionny Nauchno- Technicheski Komplex and Ukraine's Kiev Aviation Plant plan to start test flights of a new Tupolev-334 100-seat passenger jet this May if they can find the cash, the chief designer of the Tupolev complex said on Wednesday.
Igor Kalygin told a news conference that the Russian market would need 160 planes of this type in the next few years.
He said the first five Tu-334s had been assembled in Kiev but it would cost 15 billion roubles to fund test flights.
"There are no technical obstacles to beginning serial production of the jet....but we must first resolve financial problems," he said.
He said the Tu-334 would replace Tu-134 short- and medium-range jets and Yakovlev-42 planes.
"We have got 14 options for this aircraft from Russian airlines, including the Siberian Tyumenaviatrans, Komi-Avia and Moscow's Vnukovo Airlines," Kalygin told reporters.
Official Russian figures show that 208 Tu-134s and 69 Yak-42s were operating in 1997, but this was expected to fall to 139 and 35 by 2001.

Alexander Karlov, chief executive of the Kiev aviation plant, said the new plane would cost $14-15 million and have a range of 4,000 km (2,500 miles) and would offer passengers a greater degree of comfort than existing models.
Kalygin said the new plane may be fitted with Western engines and avionics on request. But a regular plane would have 70 percent Russian parts and 30 percent Ukrainian ones.
The state-owned Kiev aviation plant produces Antonov-32 military freighters and Antonov-124 cargo planes.
The Tupolev complex comprises a Moscow-based design bureau, test-flight base and several experimental production plants.

Tupolev also has agreements with plane-makers such as AO Aviastar in the Central Russian city of Ulyanovsk, Kazan aviation plant in Tatarstan and AO Aviakor in Samara which help build the planes and share the profits.
